![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14258665/assets/e41f222af118c05177c42ffdfaf2a6b4ad6ca091d62b76c36de3dacea48c20b1.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=3y-{y}^{2}$ and $x=3-y,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(y)=3y-{y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=3-y.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 3y-{y}^{2} & =3-y \\ {y}^{2}-4y+3 & =0 \\ (y-1)(y-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions in our region are $y=1$ and $y=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=1$ to $y=3.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14258665/assets/7c9e92c27d0e89f50e6d9936dbbc37f17e2093f3c65b66082fc75b15fd951cda.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=3-y,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=3y-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}y([3y-{y}^{2}]-[3-y])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}y(-3+4y-{y}^{2})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
